html:
The Battle of Jena-Auerstedt was two battles fought on the same day, 14 October 1806, about 20 km apart in Thuringia, central Germany. The French under Napoleon destroyed the army of Prussia.

Prussia had stayed out of the war of 1805. Alarmed by French power in Germany, it now went to war almost alone, before Russian help could arrive. Its army still used the methods of Frederick the Great, and its generals were old and slow. Napoleon moved north quickly and got between the Prussians and Berlin. At Jena he beat what he thought was the main army. In fact the main army, over 50,000 men with the king and the Duke of Brunswick, was at Auerstedt. There a single French corps of 27,000 under Marshal Davout fought it and won. Brunswick was fatally wounded, and both Prussian forces fled.

The army fell apart, fortresses gave up without a fight, and Napoleon entered Berlin within two weeks. In 1807 Prussia lost half its land. The shock led to deep reforms of its army, schools and laws, and an end to serfdom. That reformed Prussia later helped beat Napoleon at Leipzig and went on to unite Germany.
